utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to wish everyone a good day, and I would like the registrar to call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] IT-96-23/2-I, the Prosecutor against Mr. Stankovic [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: I would like the appearances, please. The Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, good morning. My name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff. I appear today with my colleague Mr. Sachdeva, and we are accompanied by the case manager Mr. Van Hooydonk. I think there is something wrong in the transcript because this is here the case against Mr. Gojko Jankovic and not Mr. Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you are right. It is Mr. Jankovic this morning. The indictment concerned three accused in its final draft. Mr. Stankovic has been removed from this case. There has been an amended indictment drafted as far as he is concerned, and today we shall be speaking about Mr. Jankovic. You are quite right. I didn't see this on the transcript. Registrar, could you please call the case again. The Prosecutor versus Mr. Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge El Mahdi. I shall call the case for the transcript. It is the case Prosecutor versus Gojko Jankovic, IT-96-23/2-I. Thank you, Judge El Mahdi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. This was to make sure everything was quite clear. Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff, is everything all right now?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Now the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour; good morning everyone. My name is Aleksandar Lazarevic. I am Defence counsel for Mr. Jankovic in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. You may sit down. Mr. Jankovic, can you hear me in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed. I would like to ask the Defence counsel whether he has had the opportunity to discuss these matters with his client and whether Mr. Jankovic would like to hear the entire indictment read out or should we just read out the counts of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have discussed all the issues related to the indictment with Mr. Jankovic on two occasions, and he is ready to enter his plea today. He doesn't wish the whole indictment to be read out but only the relevant parts, only the charges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Jankovic, I have clearly understood that you have discussed these matters with your counsel. We shall, therefore, just explain the counts to you this morning so that you are able to plead. Before reading out the charges, I have the duty to tell you or to give you the background against which this indictment is set. Under item -- general allegations, the charge stipulates that at all times relevant in the current indictment Bosnia-Herzegovina was the theatre of an international [as interpreted] conflict, and at all times relevant to the indictment the accused had to abide by the laws and customs of war, that unless otherwise stipulated, all acts and omissions quoted in the indictment took place between April 1992 and February of 1993, that each count in the indictment relating against crimes against humanity sanctioned for Article 5 of the Statute of the Tribunal, acts or omissions included in a general offensive on a large scale or systematic against a civilian population, i.e., the Muslim population in the municipality of Foca. After that you are held individually responsible for the crimes which are alleged against you. Also that pursuant to Article 7(3) of the Tribunal in your capacity as a superior you're alternatively criminally responsible for the acts of your subordinates, and this relates to the counts 1 to 4. In other words, the facts and omissions alleged. Allegedly committed at Buk Bijela. That said, I would like the registrar to kindly read out the counts 1 to 4 contained in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge. Count 1, torture, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(f) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you plead, Mr. Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to stipulate that these are alleged facts, and these acts have been allegedly committed in Buk Bijela because there are several locations or areas for which you are accused for having acted or omitted to act. So as regards the first four counts, these are facts or alleged omissions that were committed in Buk Bijela. Would you resume the reading, please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 2, rape, a crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jankovic, how do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty. The persons mentioned in my indictment are persons that I never had anything at all to do with, not before the war, not during the war, not after the war. We were never a single unit. They were never my army, and last but not least they were not under my command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand full well that you wish to defend yourself, but this hearing is a formal hearing, and you will be only confronted with the indictment so that you may plead either guilty or not guilty, and you will have ample time to defend your case afterwards. Shall we now move on to count number 3, please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... torture. Torture, a violation of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal and recognised by Common Article 3(1)(a), torture, of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you plead, Mr. Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could we move on to count number 4, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... rape. Rape, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you plead, Mr. Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We shall now move on to the alleged facts having been committed in the secondary school at Foca relating to counts 25, 26, 27, and 28. Mr. Registrar, could you help us here please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 25, Torture. Torture, a crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(f) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you plead, Mr. Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... rape. Rape, a crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you plead, Mr. Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... torture. Torture a violation of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal and recognised by Common Article 3(1)(a), torture, of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you plead, Mr. Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... rape. Rape, a violation of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you plead Mr. Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Jankovic. We shall now move on to the alleged acts and omissions having been committed at the Partizan Sports Hall. These relate to counts 37, 38, 39, and 40. Mr. Registrar, could you help us here, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... torture, a crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(f) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: How do you plead, Mr. Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Rape, a crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you plead, Mr. Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... torture, a violation of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal and recognised by Common Article 3(1)(a), torture, of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you plead, Mr. Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... rape, a violation of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you plead, Mr. Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We shall now move on to another location which is a flat located close to the fish shop [as interpreted] in Foca. This took place around the 30th of October, 1992. Mr. Registrar, would you kindly read out the counts 49 and 50, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued] ... rape. Rape, a crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you plead, Mr. Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Jankovic. Mr. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... rape. Rape, a violation of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you plead, Mr. Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may sit down. I believe we have met the requirements as they are stipulated in Article -- Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. I would like Mr. Registrar to set a date for the next hearing in this case, and I would like the parties, whether they have any issue they would like to raise at this stage of the proceedings. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one small matter in relation to the transcript, while the registrar actually always read out the number of the count, it's missing in the transcript. I don't know for what reason. But it just needs to be clearly stated that the number was always read out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That said, is it a particular number that was not written in here or are you talking about all the counts and count numbers?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Most of the time the count numbers that were actually read out were missing. When you mentioned them they are in the transcript, but when the registrar read out as mentioned here it's often missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I can confirm that as regards the transcripts, all counts have been read out and that Mr. Jankovic, in respect to each of these counts, stated that he was not guilty. I can repeat the count numbers, counts ranging from 1 to 4, after which we have counts 25, 26, 27, and 28, and we have counts 37, 38, 39, 40, and lastly counts 49 and 50. For each count, Mr. Jankovic, after having read these counts, stated that he was not guilty. I think it is quite clear now, isn't it? What do you think?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And nothing else is ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for the relevant comment you made. The Defence, do you have any issue you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... raise any issue. We have nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Lazarevic. Before adjourning this hearing, I would like to repeat what is contained in the indictment as regards the forced -- the first four counts. You are held responsible on an individual basis and also on the basis of your position, i.e., that you were the superior of your subordinates. That said, the hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: adjourned at 9.29 a.m.
